text: Microsoft’s Recall feature became a privacy scandal in 2024 because it was initially designed as an AI "memory" tool that automatically screenshotted the user's screen every few seconds and stored this data locally [Source: ev-1]. The changed version of Recall is now opt-in (default OFF) rather than enabled by default [Source: ev-1]. Additionally, accessing the timeline requires Windows Hello authentication and presence detection, and the feature explicitly excludes incognito browsing sessions and DRM content [Source: ev-1]. While this revised, more secure version reached general availability on Copilot+ PCs in 2025, the initial controversy permanently shaped privacy conversations surrounding AI PCs [Source: ev-1].
